implementation_notes: The Kotlin stdlib offers no error accumulation: Result<T> is a discriminated union over a single Throwable and runCatching is fail-fast, so the pattern is hand-written - a sealed hierarchy of violations plus a Notification with a MutableList and add/hasErrors, or a data class carrying the list. Prefer the sealed type over strings so the presentation can map codes exhaustively; use the Arrow variant when the validation should compose applicatively.
pitfalls: kotlin.Result carries a Throwable and is meant for fail-fast boundaries; using it as an accumulated validation result hides the failures inside one exception.
Exposing the backing MutableList lets callers mutate the notification - return a read-only copy from the accessor.
One data-class object per failure allocates; on hot paths prefer an enum/error-code plus field string.

variants.name: Arrow zipOrAccumulate
variants.implementation_notes: Arrow makes the choice explicit: ensure/bind inside either {} short-circuits on the first raised problem, while zipOrAccumulate runs the independent per-field validations and collects them into a NonEmptyList on the Left - the documentation's own framing is 'notify the user about all the problems found in the form at once'. Use the accumulating form for input validation and the plain either {} form when later checks need earlier values.
pitfalls: zipOrAccumulate is for independent checks; using it for a check that needs the previous value hides the dependency and can raise on unparsed input.
The error side is a NonEmptyList, so mapping it back to a single sealed type needs toList()/reduce at the boundary.
Mixing raise() (short-circuit) with zipOrAccumulate in one either block is legal but reads as if all checks accumulate - keep the two styles in separate functions.
